deck_title: Boussinesq-Cerruti 1/r elastic half-space Green function subsidence vs naive unattenuated Winkler plateau sink rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Joseph Boussinesq (1885) & Valentino Cerruti (1882) 3D Navier-Cauchy elastic half-space surface Green function (vertical surface displacement w_B(r) = ((1 - nu) / (2 * pi * G)) * (F / r) = w_0 / (1 + u) decaying inversely with radial distance r(u) = r_0 * (1 + u) so r * w_B(r) = const, locking w_active / w_B = 1.0000x across all 17 radial stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive unattenuated Winkler plateau depression (w = w_0, which over-sinks the collar by r / r_0 = 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer vertical strain quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Giant mech/kaiju footstep ground subsidence, soft mattress/sofa cushion indentation, and heavy vehicle terrain heightmap shaders
Applying the Boussinesq 1/r half-space Green kernel w(r) = w_0 / sqrt(1 + (r/r_c)^2) so surrounding ground slopes smoothly toward the load center instead of punching cookie-cutter step cliffs
Superposing multiple contact loads F_i on a GPU heightmap in O(1) per contact via linear elasticity
not_for: Dry cohesionless sand avalanches governed by Coulomb angle-of-repose plastic slumping
